name: lattice
title: A lattice spring block: re-entrant cells between two plates
orientation: Flat on the bed on its face, one piece, no supports: the cells lie in the bed's plane, so every wall bends within its layers. Press it between its plates, along y.

block.label: The block: two plates and the cells between them

load.rule: The design load the block springs under: 5 N takes it 0.98 mm, and its walls may go 2.03 mm before PETG's strain limit (2.06 times the margin)

slant.rule: Each slanted wall's length, centreline to centreline: longer walls bend further for a strain

upright.rule: Each upright wall's length: over 2 × 10 × sin 20° = 6.84 mm, so a cell's top and bottom points stay apart

angle.rule: The slanted walls lean 20 degrees inwards (re-entrant): the sides draw in when pressed, and the walls see less strain for a press than a plain honeycomb's

thickness.rule: Every wall: two lines, the thinnest that prints solid

depth.rule: The block's height off the bed: 30 layers. Stiffness and buckling force grow with it, the strain for a travel does not

across.rule: Whole cells along x, with half cells at the sides of the rows between

rows.rule: Cell rows from plate to plate: four rows carry the travel, so each wall's share is a quarter

plate.rule: Each solid plate's thickness: far stiffer than the walls, and flat to press on
